records.rationale: Omit the protected-guest detector and its config/build/enum registration. Complete patch requires the distinct PKVMPKVMPKVM CPUID signature, which ACK supplies only for protected vCPUs in its private hypervisor. The SDK deliverable is the ordinary Goldfish/QEMU guest; launching this kernel itself as an x86 protected guest is a separate deployment not claimed here. ACK GKI does enable this config, so omission is deliberate target scope, not a claim the feature was absent. Keep all native hypervisor detection and KVM guest support. A different outer VMM/CPUID contract requires reassessment; the SDK command line alone does not establish its CPUID.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit protected-guest memory ownership sharing: page touching, share retry on EAGAIN, unshare errors, confidential-computing vendor attributes and set_memory interception. These are coupled to the protected detector and host ownership hypercalls. Keep whole native CoCo/PAT/memory-encryption files and their LTS locking/errors. Ordinary virtio transport/DMA remains available. Do not advertise protected memory isolation without this backend; no pKVM guest or arbitrary outer VMM compatibility is claimed.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit protected-only MMIO hypercalls and all read/write callbacks. They exist to emulate accesses when the host cannot read protected guest instructions. The entire private implementation is absent; ordinary native inline MMIO and barrier semantics are retained, including full native io.h/paravirt files. Its later present-entry validation fix is assessed separately, not silently discarded while retaining the vulnerable function.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit the six protected-guest PCI MMCONFIG callback overrides with the protected MMIO backend. Full patch only assigns read/write b/w/l callbacks during protected-guest initialization. Native PCI access and MMIO primitives are retained; no independent generic PCI fix is lost. A guest protected from its outer host is outside this SDK deployment.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit protected-guest secondary-CPU hypercall registration. Full patch replaces the APIC wakeup callback only inside protected-guest initialization, where host-emulated INIT/SIPI is not trusted. Retain native APIC startup and mitigations for the ordinary SDK. This does not promise trusted CPU startup under pKVM or restore the untrusted APIC method inside a supported protected guest.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit the x86 pKVM-specific balloon-disable stub and architecture capability selection. They are necessary for the separate protected guest lacking relinquish support, and are omitted with that guest backend. Entire native virtio core and balloon files remain, including clearing ACCESS_PLATFORM and rejecting restricted-memory devices lacking it; the ACK relaxation 5444ed1c069f is not imported. Thus the known protected balloon hazard is not newly enabled. Ordinary SDK balloon module remains compiled.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit the static-key MMIO optimization with the already excluded pv_mmio_ops introduction f87819dc9429. Full patch improves ordinary systems affected by ACK indirect dispatch, but the port retains the whole native inline mov accessors and has no such dispatch overhead to fix. No key/export is needed without the backend; native barrier and call semantics remain. Do not transplant older ACK paravirt implementation over LTS.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

records.rationale: Omit the unsigned lookup level and hardware-present check only because the complete private pkvm_virt_mmio implementation is absent. This is a real correctness/security fix: non-present metadata must not become a physical address passed to the hypervisor, and PROTNONE must not count as hardware-present. No older vulnerable copy is retained. If protected-guest MMIO is added later, both fixes are required along with its ownership/translation contract.
evidence: SECURITY.md: X86 protected guest boundary and native MMIO

method: All eight complete original patches read; all 15 affected final paths compared as whole blobs, plus native virtio and paravirt types. Native MMIO and virtio restricted-memory negotiation read; ACK detector and protected-host CPUID producer traced. Pinned Goldfish artifact/command-line files and AVF protected VM launch branching examined.
limits: SDK ordinary guest is the deployment boundary, not a runtime observation of CPUID. ACK GKI enables PKVM_X86_GUEST; excluded deliberately. AVF has real protected-VM consumers, as its explicit crosvm protectedVm branch demonstrates. No outer hypervisor, guest memory sharing, CPU startup, or protected/nested VM runtime was tested. Failed old-path lookups and broad file searches are not absence evidence. Commit-message URLs were not contacted.
